chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked: “For what reason is the deceased washed?” He said:
The drop from which he was created comes out of him, emerging from his eyes or from his mouth, and no one departs from this world until he sees his place in Paradise or in the Fire.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the present worldly life from which the soul departs at death
key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire, the abode of punishment shown to some at death
key_terms.النُّطْفَةُ: the seminal drop from which the human being was created
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the abode of reward shown to some at death
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased person whose body is washed after death

ai.seo_question: Why is the deceased given ghusl in Shia hadith, and what does a person see at the time of death?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a reason for performing ghusl (ritual bath) for the deceased, linking it to what exits from the body at death. It also teaches that at the moment of departure from the world, a person is shown their place in either Paradise or the Fire.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.375 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked: "For what reason is the deceased washed (given ghusl)?"
Imam ( as) said:
"The drop that he was created from, exits from their eyes or their mouth, and no one leaves this world until they see their place in either Paradise or the Fire."
